model: uncertainty -> experiment -> information gained -> technical decision -> capital avoided/unlocked (directive section 17)
dominant_uncertainty: Whether the floor lumen survives the dominant clinical obstruction mechanisms (common-cause failure) and carries a clinically meaningful minimum flow. This is the package's own recorded CRITICAL unknown (MATURITY_BASIS known_blockers: 'Whether floor is genuinely immune to common-cause obstruction — UNKNOWN (critical)'; 'Optimal Q_min for clinical safety — UNKNOWN').

uncertainty_inventory.uncertainty: Common-cause obstruction immunity of the floor lumen
uncertainty_inventory.class: MECHANISM_LEVEL (kills the concept if resolved negatively)
uncertainty_inventory.information_gained_if_run: Binary kill-or-survive on the mechanism's central premise plus measured common-cause rate per obstruction class
uncertainty_inventory.decision_it_changes: Whether ANY further development money is spent on this technology at all
uncertainty_inventory.capital_at_stake: The entire downstream development chain (prototype, preclinical, regulatory, clinical) is avoidable if the mechanism dies at the bench — the experiment is the cheapest possible gate in front of that chain

uncertainty_inventory.resolvable_by: Pre-registered clinical-literature derivation (part of the decisive experiment protocol, owner-gated)
uncertainty_inventory.information_gained_if_run: An acceptance threshold with provenance (Art. XXVII CLINICAL/BUYER_DEFINED class) instead of an unset endpoint
uncertainty_inventory.decision_it_changes: Whether the primary endpoint is decidable at all; without it the experiment cannot produce an ACCEPT

uncertainty_inventory.class: MANUFACTURING (gates prototype stage, not the concept)
uncertainty_inventory.resolvable_by: Vendor extrusion quote + sample run (standard micro-extrusion feasibility study)
uncertainty_inventory.information_gained_if_run: Manufacturability verdict and cost envelope for the 0.6 mm floor lumen at 0.2 mm min wall
uncertainty_inventory.decision_it_changes: Whether PROTOTYPE_DEVELOPMENT is enterable after a positive experiment

uncertainty_inventory.uncertainty: Regulatory pathway (510(k) predicate vs De Novo)
uncertainty_inventory.resolvable_by: Regulatory consultant review of predicate landscape
uncertainty_inventory.information_gained_if_run: Pathway class + rough submission cost/time envelope
uncertainty_inventory.decision_it_changes: Total program cost estimate; does not gate the decisive experiment

cheapest_decisive_action: The bench obstruction experiment (DECISIVE_EXPERIMENT.json) is the highest information-gain per unit cost: it attacks the mechanism-level uncertainty directly, requires no human subjects, no regulatory path, and its negative outcome terminates the program at the lowest possible sunk cost (Constitution Art. LVI: information gain per unit cost, not document count).
what_a_buyer_buys_by_funding_it: The disappearance of the mechanism-level uncertainty: after the experiment, the buyer knows whether the safety-floor premise physically survives the obstruction classes that dominate clinical failure — regardless of which way the result points. That is strictly more valuable than any technology score: the negative result is worth the entire avoided development chain.
explicit_not_claimed: No monetary VOI figure is computed — a credible one requires the Q_min literature derivation and vendor cost inputs (owner actions); inventing a number here would violate Constitution Art. XXVII (no threshold invention) and Art. VI (never manufacture provenance)
next_information_gain_order: 1. Q_min literature derivation (unlocks the endpoint) — owner action
2. Bench obstruction experiment (kills or survives the mechanism) — the decisive contract
3. Extrusion feasibility (gates prototype) — only after a positive experiment outcome
4. Regulatory pathway review (gates program costing) — parallel, non-blocking
